overall_summary: The performance data sample size is extremely small, with view counts ranging between 5 and 20 views and no engagement recorded yet. Confidence is low, meaning we cannot rely on definitive winners. However, topics involving personal phones, numbers, and late-night relational echoes (रिश्ते, ओवरथिंकिंग) showed marginally higher traction, indicating an audience resonance with modern digital relationship anxiety.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on phone contact names and saved numbers ('आज भी फोन में तुम्हारा नाम सुरक्षित है') garnered the highest views in the set (20 views).
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing on micro-interactions related to smartphones and digital artifacts of old relationships.

weak_patterns.evidence: Openings like 'रात के दो बजे' or 'मेज पर रखी चाय' performed lower (5-12 views) due to cliché phrasing.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract time/weather setups and immediately ground the hook in a specific physical or digital action.

next_video.concept: Checking an old chat archive just to see if they were online last.
next_video.opening_direction: Scroll karne laga toh socha, bas ek baar dekh lu ki wo aakhri baar kab online aayi thi.
next_video.twist_direction: Pata chala last seen hide hai, aur samajh aa gaya ki ab hum sirf ek purani history bankar reh gaye hain.
next_video.reason: Evening hours capture the peak time when users experience high overthinking and quiet reflection regarding broken ties.

experiment: Testing a specific digital behavior hook (checking last seen status) instead of broader contact name themes to improve watch time and comment engagement.
